comparison_arms: Littermate WT, HT, KO layer II/III pyramidal neurons from the same slice batches; each cell held at one common potential by bias current and stepped to the same peak potential (current scaled per cell); additional arm at the original fixed -200 pA; arm with and arm without synaptic blockers; identity by morphology or marker; access resistance, bridge balance and capacitance reported by genotype; seal and access resistance reported per cell so that smaller cells plus a fixed seal leak (A10) can be separated from a conductance difference
readouts: Sag and rebound at matched potential and deflection; sag ratio normalised to peak deflection; Rin from a declared current range; tau; capacitance from the voltage-clamp transient
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Excess sag and rebound vanish at matched conditions: passive and conductance-level reading (MH1). Excess persists: non-passive contribution (MH2). Contrast shrinks under blockade or with matched Ra or identity: state or selection artefact (MH3, A05, A06)
cost_note: Slice electrophysiology with existing equipment; animals not cells are the replicate (5, 6, 15 animals in the paper); no drug
existing_module_step_reused: hcn_20261107 experiment.tsv X1 (extended with blockade, Ra and capacitance)

comparison_arms: Voltage clamp in the same neurons: Ih as the ZD7288-sensitive current and, in a separate cell set, the ivabradine-sensitive current, with time-matched run-down controls and a sodium-current check at the ZD7288 concentration used
readouts: Ih amplitude and density per pF, V1/2, slope, kinetics, tail current
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Same density and V1/2: no HCN difference. Larger density or shifted V1/2: HCN differs; both chemotypes must agree before assigning the current to HCN
cost_note: Voltage clamp on small neurons in slices is limited by space clamp; at P13-P17 dendritic Ih is under-clamped

comparison_arms: Difference current in KO versus WT: I-V of the Ba2+-sensitive (and, separately, XE991-sensitive) current from about -120 to -60 mV, junction potential corrected, with E_K computed for the actual solutions
readouts: Zero-crossing of the difference current; conductance at rest; Ba2+ and XE991 effects on rest and Rin in each genotype
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Difference reverses near E_K and is smaller in KO: K+ leak or Kv7 conductance is smaller (still not an identification of the channel). No reversal near E_K: the conductance difference is something else or there is no leak difference. A blocker effect equal in WT and KO shows no genotype-specific role
cost_note: Needs the junction offset measured; Ba2+ blocks other K+ channels (Kir, K2P in part); a response to a blocker is not a defect

comparison_arms: Bath ZD7288 and ivabradine, each alone, with a Z944 arm and a Kv7 arm run separately in WT, HT, KO; engagement shown first by sag removal; vehicle and wash-out controls
readouts: Sag, rebound, Rin, rest, firing, AP height; burst incidence in the same bursting KO slices
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Sag removed and bursts unchanged: HCN shapes sag, not bursts. Bursts fall: candidate role in the network, still tool-level. Bursts rise: not by itself compensation without off-target and compartment checks
cost_note: Needs bursting KO slices (36 of 42 in the paper); non-specific suppression control

comparison_arms: Age series (for example P10, P13, P17) and layer V in addition to layer II/III, with morphology-based identity
readouts: Rin, rest, tau, capacitance, sag by age, layer and genotype
what_each_outcome_would_mean: Differences present at all ages and in both layers: cell-autonomous and stable; present only at one age: maturation-stage effect; sag falling with delay in mutants: immaturity pattern (A04)
cost_note: Breeding cost for an age series; KO dies at weeks 3-4
